key_insight: You can align frozen vision and language models with high-quality cross-modal correspondences using optimal transport and only a small fraction of paired data by leveraging unpaired data in a semi‑supervised framework.
problem_solved: Reduces the reliance on millions of paired image–text examples for aligning unimodal pretrained models, enabling efficient cross-modal alignment with far less supervision.
method: Compute distributional correspondences between vision and language embedding clouds using optimal transport to obtain soft matchings (transport plans) between modalities.

Train lightweight alignment layers on top of frozen unimodal encoders in a semi‑supervised setup: supervise alignment with a small set of paired examples and regularize with OT-based distribution alignment using abundant unpaired samples.
Iteratively refine alignment by combining local supervised losses (paired points) and global OT objectives to produce coherent, low-cost cross-modal mappings.
impact: Makes multimodal alignment practical when paired data is scarce, lowering annotation costs and enabling fast adaptation of pretrained encoders for downstream cross-modal retrieval, transfer, or multi‑modal reasoning tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side latent-space diagram showing vision and language embedding clouds with OT transport lines (thicker lines = stronger matches).
Semi-supervised data schematic: few solid paired links between modalities plus many unpaired points contributing to a global OT alignment.
Before/after performance bar or line chart illustrating improved alignment quality or retrieval accuracy as paired data decreases.
Icon set: lightweight adapter layer, Earth Mover's Distance/OT symbol, and a data-efficiency badge (e.g., small dataset icon).
paper_title: SOTAlign: Semi-Supervised Alignment of Unimodal Vision and Language Models via Optimal Transport
paper_authors: Simon Roschmann, Paul Krzakala, Sonia Mazelet, Quentin Bouniot, Zeynep Akata
